key_insight: A physics-constrained, multi-fidelity ML augmentation of Spalart–Allmaras can make turbulence modeling cost scale formally as O(log(Re)) while preserving accuracy across Reynolds numbers.
engineering_relevance: This offers a practical path to cheaper high-Re CFD predictions for wall-bounded flows by training at affordable low-Re conditions and transferring to higher-Re cases.
method: Field inversion + machine learning on top of Spalart–Allmaras
Constrained formulation that preserves the law of the wall
Train at low Re, then deploy and test at higher Re for extrapolation
evidence_signal: The abstract reports successful transfer from channel flow at Re_tau=1000 to Re_tau=5200 and from periodic hill training at Re_b=5600 to tests at Re_b=10595, 19000, and 37000, with the constrained model giving the lowest RMSE and nearly Re-independent error.
watch_item: The formal O(log(Re)) claim depends on assumptions such as mean-flow-aligned grids, fixed spanwise resolution, and steady-solver cost scaling linearly with grid points, so performance may change outside those conditions.
paper_title: A formal log(Re)-cost framework for the engineering turbulence problem
